name: Hyperbolic Tiling
desc: A Poincare-disk hyperbolic tessellation in the spirit of Escher's Circle Limit, its {p,q} jewel-toned tiles shrinking in infinite regress toward the boundary while a slow Mobius drift and elliptic spin make them stream endlessly outward, rendered as backlit stained glass, carved woodcut, a glowing neon lattice, or two-tone op-art moire.

scale.doc: hyperbolic zoom / disk size (small framed disk .. big tiles filling frame)

warp.doc: static Mobius push strength (0=centred symmetric .. 1=tiles crammed hard to one side)

speed.doc: spin + Mobius drift rate (0 keeps a base spin floor alive)

density.doc: regress depth + thinner geodesic leading (chunky .. fine infinite detail)

valence.doc: q in {p,q} - polygons per vertex (auto-bumped until 1/p+1/q<1/2)

glow.doc: central backlight + limit-circle rim glow width

style.doc: render philosophy: matte jewel mass with dark leading / backlit leaded glass / carved black-on-cream woodcut print / edge-only additive neon wireframe / flat two-tone optical moire

act.doc: dramaturgy: streaming Mobius drift+spin / calm pure elliptic spin / deeper pulsing infinite-zoom dive
